(4) Paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 5 and paragraph 1 of Article 6 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1309 of the European Parliament and of the Council are not applied when granting access to information concerning the planning of building work and to construction works whose construction does not require the filing of a building notice or the issue of a building permit, as well as to construction works that serve national defence purposes, to construction works of the security authorities and to infrastructure at the national border.
[RT I, 21.11.2025, 1 – entry into force 12.05.2026]

§ 82². Right to access construction works owned by the state or municipality
(1) A communications undertaking may file, by electronic means via the Register of Construction Works, an application to the state or municipality for access to a construction work owned by the state or municipality in order to install an active device of a mobile telephone network, including a base station and the antennae connected to it as well as a small-area wireless access point.
(2) The state or municipality may only require the owner of the active device of the mobile telephone network to compensate the costs that arise in relation to installing the active device mentioned in subsection 1 of this section, to its continued use and to its removal.
(3) The application mentioned in subsection 1 of this section must contain the following:
1) contact particulars of the communications undertaking;
2) the location, including coordinates, for installation of the active device of the mobile telephone network;
3) a technical drawing of the installation of the active device.
(4) The state or municipality decides the grant of access to install the active device of the mobile telephone network within two months following reception of the corresponding application. Decisions are made in the order the applications were filed.
(5) The state or municipality may refuse access to install the active device of the mobile telephone network where:
1) the construction work is not suited, technically or because of its architecture, for installation of the active device;
2) this endangers the life or health of humans;
3) the construction work is a building mentioned in clauses 1 and 2 of subsection 2 of § 62 of this Code;
4) this represents a threat to national security;
5) the construction work does not have sufficient space for installation of the active device;
6) the construction work is connected to the integrity and safety of the infrastructure required for provision of a vital service.
(6) The decisions made under subsections 4 and 5 of this section are presented electronically via the Register of Construction Works. The decisions made under subsections 4 and 5 of this section, with the exception of decisions made on the ground mentioned in clause 4 of subsection 5, are made public in the Register.
[RT I, 21.11.2025, 1 – entry into force 12.05.2026]

§ 83. Design specifications
(1) Design specifications are required:
1) in relation to a communications construction work – with the exception of lines – for the creation of building design documentation concerning a new line civil engineering work;
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
2) for the construction of a new electrical installation that is subject to the building permit obligation and that traverses two or more items of immovable property or
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
3) for increasing the nominal voltage of an existing electrical installation to 110 kilovolts or more.
(2) Design specifications are not issued if the building of the construction work mentioned in subsection 1 of this section is prescribed by a detailed spatial plan or a national or municipal designated spatial plan.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]

§ 84. Resolution of disputes arising in relation to communications construction works
(1) When resolving disputes arising in relation to communications construction works, the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority takes guidance from the provisions established in § 149 of Electronic Communications Act.
(2) Disputes arising in relation to communications construction works must be resolved within six months.
(3) In the case of disputes relating to very high capacity communication networks, the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority serves as the national dispute settlement body within the meaning of Article 14 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1309 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
[RT I, 21.11.2025, 1 - entry into force 01.01.2026]

§ 84¹. Building permit for a thermal power station
(1) In relation to the building or remodelling of a thermal power station, the application for the building permit is filed together with an analysis that meets the requirements of § 10 of the Energy Sector Organisation Act of the costs and benefits of turning the thermal power station into an efficient cogeneration plant, if such an analysis is required under that section.
(2) The building permit applied for in order to build or remodel a thermal power station is not granted if the building design documentation of the electrical installation of the thermal power station to be built or remodelled does not conform to a positive result of the analysis of costs and benefits mentioned in subsection 1 of this section.
[RT I, 05.07.2016, 3 - entry into force 15.07.2016]

§ 84². Building notice for solar energy equipment with a capacity below 100 kilowatts
Where, in building notice proceedings for the construction – as a civil engineering work or as a utility system – of solar energy equipment with a capacity below 100 kilowatts, the competent authority, having initiated the verification provided for by subsection 5 of § 36 of this Code, has not issued an administrative decision within the time-limit prescribed by subsection 6 of § 36, building work may commence.
[RT I, 18.03.2026, 1 – entry into force 28.03.2026]

§ 85. Use and occupancy notice and use and occupancy permit
(1) Where, in order to begin using a construction work, a use and occupancy notice must be filed or a use and occupancy permit is required, and where the construction work or an installation in the construction work is subject to an audit or inspection requirement, the use and occupancy notice or the application for a use and occupancy permit must be accompanied by an opinion that results from a pre-use audit or from an inspection and that shows the construction work or installation to be in conformity with the requirements.
[RT I, 30.06.2020, 2 - entry into force 01.01.2021]
(2) [Repealed – RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]


Chapter 10 Railway Civil Engineering Works

§ 86. Scope of application
The provisions in this Chapter apply to railway civil engineering works.

§ 87. Requirements for use and maintenance
In addition to the requirements arising from this Code, the use and maintenance of railway civil engineering works is subject to the requirements arising from the Railways Act.
[RT I, 30.10.2020, 1 - entry into force 31.10.2020]

§ 88. Design specifications
(1) The creation of building design documentation concerning a railway civil engineering work that is subject to the building permit requirement and that is mentioned in Annex 1 to this Code Design requires corresponding design specifications, except where such a civil engineering work is to be demolished.
(2) Design specifications for a railway civil engineering work are issued by the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority.
[RT I, 30.10.2020, 1 - entry into force 31.10.2020]
(3) Approval for design specifications for a railway civil engineering work must be obtained from the municipality concerned.
[RT I, 30.10.2020, 1 - entry into force 31.10.2020]

§ 89. Building notice and building permit
To build a railway civil engineering work, a building notice is filed with the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority or a building permit is issued by the Authority.
[RT I, 30.10.2020, 1 - entry into force 31.10.2020]

§ 90. Use and occupancy notice and use and occupancy permit
In order to start using a railway civil engineering work, the use and occupancy notice is filed with the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority who also issues the use and occupancy permit.
[RT I, 30.10.2020, 1 - entry into force 31.10.2020]


Chapter 11 Roads

§ 91. Scope of application
(1) The requirements in this Chapter apply to public roads and to private roads accessible to the public. Of the requirements provided by this Chapter, only those of § 93 apply to forest roads.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(2) The provisions on the Register of Construction Works may be applied to the building, design and maintenance of roads as well as to any related activities.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]

§ 92. Definitions
(1) ‘Road’ means a civil engineering work that is intended for the movement or traffic of humans, vehicles or animals. Tunnels, bridges, overpasses and other civil engineering works used for traffic and required for the functioning of the road are regard as parts of the road.
(2) ‘Highway’ means a road that is situated outside cities, towns or small towns and that is intended for vehicle and pedestrian traffic.
(3) ‘Street’ means a road that is situated in a city, town or small town.
(4) A road may consist of different road types.
(5) ‘Public road’ means a national road, local road and a private road designated for public use. Public roads may be used by everybody while observing the restrictions established in legislation.
(6) [Repealed – RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(7) [Repealed – RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(8) ‘Private road accessible to the public’ means a road that has a public function as determined by its owner and that is not a national or local road.
(9) ‘Roads of the trans-European road network’ means roads identified by Regulation (EU) No 2024/1679 of the European Parliament and of the Council on Union guidelines for the development of the trans-European transport network, amending Regulations (EU) 2021/1153 and (EU) No 913/2010 and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1315/2013 (OJ L, 2024/1679, 28.06.2024).
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(10) The minister in charge of the policy sector enacts, by regulation, definitions of the terms related to the building and maintenance of roads and the location, in Estonian territory, of roads of the trans-European road network.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]

§ 92¹. National roads
(1) ’National road’ means a road owned by the state and designated as national road, or a private road designated as public road by the state. For national roads, the duties of the owner are performed by the Transport Administration.
(2) A road is designated as national road if it possesses the core characteristics of national roads – which first and foremost consist in the serving of international traffic and in ensuring a connection between the state’s various geographical areas as well as destinations of broad public interest or economic impact – and having regard to the road’s engineering solution, the nature of the traffic served and the general principle of ensuring unified traffic and road maintenance organisation on national roads.
(3) A road is designated as national road by an administrative decision of the Transport Administration.
(4) The types of national roads are enacted by a regulation of the minister in charge of the policy sector.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]

§ 92². Allowing for construction of electronic communications infrastructure as part of national roads
The road management plan mentioned in subsection 1 of § 1¹ of the Road Traffic Act makes provision for expenditure on construction of passive elements of the electronic communications network that are not required for the functioning of the road, except where this is not possible due to road safety requirements and on the condition that, for operating and managing such elements, a corresponding contract has been concluded with the foundation or electronic communications undertaking managing the network.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]

§ 92³. Local roads
’Local road’ means a road that belongs to the municipality and is needed for the organisation of local road traffic or for the performance of other municipal tasks provided by subsections 1–2¹ of § 6 of the Local Government Organisation Act, or a private road that the municipality has dedicated to public use. A local road is designated by an administrative decision of the municipality. For local roads, the duties of the owner are performed by the municipality.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]

§ 93. Forest roads
(1) ‘Forest road’ means a road that is situated on land retained in the ownership of the state and that is used predominantly for the management of public forests. A forest road may be used by anyone, unless the person or government agency who arranges the management of public forests has closed the forest road or a part of the road or restricted traffic on the road.
(2) The person or government agency who arranges the management of public forests is authorised to enter into agreements concerning the use of forest roads and to arrange for the upkeep of such roads.
(3) The minister in charge of the policy sector enacts, by regulation, the requirements for the condition of forest roads.
(4) A forest road must be marked by a name or indication.
(5) The person or government agency who arranges the management of public forests arranges for the building and upkeep of forest roads.
(6) The person or government agency who arranges the management of public forests may close a forest road or a part of the road or restrict traffic on the road:
1) if the load-bearing part of the road has deteriorated due to the thawing of the ground, or due to rain or other factors that significantly affect traffic - and traffic may damage the road, or traffic on the road is dangerous;
2) for the purpose of fire safety;
3) for the purpose of protecting the ecosystems of the forest;
4) for the purpose of preventing the commission of an offence;
5) for the purpose of ensuring safety during forestry work or
6) if the road is not needed for the management of public forests or for local traffic.
(7) In order to close the forest road or restrict traffic, the person or government agency who arranges the management of public forests must install the required traffic control devices.
(8) The minister in charge of the policy sector may enact, by means of a regulation, the requirements for the marking of forest roads and the rules for the road marking system.

§ 94. Acquisition of private roads in the public interest or appropriation of private roads for public use
[RT I, 29.06.2018, 1 - entry into force 01.07.2018]
(1) A private road is designated for public use by the state or by the municipality in whose administrative territory the private road is situated.
(2) Acquisition of a private road in the public interest or subjection of a private road to compulsory possession is decided, in accordance with the rules provided by the Acquisition of Immovables in Public Interest Act, by the state or by the municipality in whose administrative territory the private road is situated.
[RT I, 29.06.2018, 1 - entry into force 01.07.2018]
(3) When a private road is designated for public use, the state or municipality assumes all obligations, rights and liability of the owner of the road. It is possible to stipulate, by a regulatory contract, that the obligations, rights and liability of the owner of the road remain vested in the owner of the private road.
[RT I, 29.06.2018, 1 - entry into force 01.07.2018]
(4) Within 7 days from the entry into effect of the decision on designating a private road for public use, the state or municipality presents that decision and, in machine-readable form, the data concerning the road’s spatial dimensions, to the keeper of the Land Cadastre.
[RT I, 29.06.2018, 1 - entry into force 01.07.2018]

§ 95. Right of pre-emption
(1) Where an item of immovable property is sold that is traversed by an existing or envisaged road that, according to the detailed spatial plan, is to be designated for public use, the municipality in whose administrative territory the item is situated has a right of pre-emption.
(2) The municipality does not have a right of pre-emption where the item of property is sold to the owner's spouse, descendant, or parent, as well as to the owner's brother, sister, or any of their descendants or to the Republic of Estonia, as well as where the property that is sold constitutes apartment ownership rights, the right of superficies or the right of apartment superficies.
(3) A note concerning the fact that the item of immovable property has been encumbered with the right of pre-emption mentioned in subsection 1 of this section is recorded in the third division of the Land Register entry for the item on an application by the municipality that brought into effect the detailed spatial plan that provides for designating the existing or envisaged road for public use. The recording of the note does not require the consent of the owner of the property. The application and the recorded note must cite this Code and this section and the detailed spatial plan that provides for designating the existing or envisaged road for public use.
(4) Where the entry in the Land Register shows that the item of immovable property is encumbered with a right of pre-emption within the meaning of this section, the notary public, within five business days from authenticating the sales or other agreement that stipulates the obligation to acquire or transfer the item, transmits a notarially certified copy of the agreement by electronic means to the municipality in whose administrative territory the item or construction work that is being sold is situated, in order for the municipality to decide on the exercise of the right of pre-emption.
(5) The right of pre-emption provided by this section may not be exercised in respect of an item of property that is sold by way of compulsory enforcement or as part of insolvency proceedings, as well as where the item of immovable property is subjected to acquisition in the public interest, including to compulsory acquisition. Where an auction is to be held in respect of an item of immovable property whose entry in the Land Register shows that it is encumbered with a right of pre-emption within the meaning of this section, the enforcement agent or trustee in bankruptcy transmits, at least ten days before the auction is held, the corresponding notice to the municipality in whose administrative territory the property is situated.
[RT I, 29.06.2018, 1 - entry into force 01.07.2018]

§ 96. Requirements for the building of roads
(1) The building or designing of tunnels whose length exceeds 500 metres is based on the requirements provied by Directive 2004/54/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on minimum safety requirements for tunnels in the trans-European road network (OJ L 167, 30.04.2004, pp. 39–91).
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(2) The minister in charge of the policy sector may, by means of a regulation, enact the requirements for the building and designing of tunnels whose length exceeds 500 metres and to designate the authority responsible for ensuring the safety of the tunnel.
(3) The minister in charge of the policy sector enacts, by means of a regulation, the quality requirements for the building of roads.

§ 97. Road maintenance
(1) Roads and any civil engineering works required for the functioning of the road must be maintained such that they conform to the requirements and such that the conditions for safe traffic are ensured.
(2) The minister in charge of the policy sector enacts, by regulation, the requirements for the condition of roads.
(3) At level crossings, building and maintenance work on the intersection is performed and conditions for safe traffic are ensured by the owner of the road, the railway infrastructure manager or the owner or possessor of the railway within the extent of the item of immovable property in their possession, except for winter maintenance work that the owner of the road is under a duty perform for the entire area of the level crossing. The owner of the road, the railway infrastructure manager or any other owner or possessor of the railway conclude an agreement that stipulates the details pertaining to winter maintenance work.
(3¹) Where a bridge or overpass that is part of a road that does not possess the core characteristics of national roads has been constructed for crossing a public railway whose track gauge is 1435 mm, the duties of the owner of the bridge or overpass are performed by the Transport Administration. Regarding the section of road mentioned in the first sentence of this subsection, compliance of the road with requirements for its condition is ensured by the municipality – if obligations with regard to ensuring compliance of the section with requirements for its condition have not been allocated between the parties on the basis of an agreement to be concluded between the Transport Administration and the municipality.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(4) At the crossing of roads belonging to different owners, each owner is responsible, within their item of immovable property, for the condition of the road that is necessary for ensuring safe traffic.
(5) The upkeep of a non-road civil engineering work, including a soil amelioration or hydro-technical civil engineering work, that is situated within the road and that is owned by another person is ensured by the owner of the non-road civil engineering work, which does not preclude liability of the owner of the road to the person who sustained harm due to the non-conformity of the road to the requirements for road condition. The owner of the non-road civil engineering work is liable to compensate the owner of the road in accordance with the rules established in the Law of Obligations Act.
(6) In a city, town and small town, the owner of the land adjacent to the road must arrange the clearing of the pavement that runs between their item of immovable property and the carriageway, including snow clearing and gritting to an extent that allows for safe pedestrian traffic on the pavement.
(7) The undertaking that maintains a national road is deemed a provider of the vital service mentioned in clause 4 of subsection 1¹ of § 36 of the Emergency Act.
[RT I, 30.06.2023, 1 - entry into force 01.07.2023]
(8) The undertaking that maintains a local road is deemed a provider of the vital service mentioned in clause 2 of subsection 4 of § 36 of the Emergency Act.
[RT I, 08.10.2024, 1 - entry into force 18.10.2024]
(9) The undertaking that maintains a local road is deemed a provider of services of general economic interest for the purposes of the General Part of the Economic Activities Code Act.
[RT I, 03.03.2017, 1 - entry into force 01.07.2017]

§ 98. Owner oversight
When building a road subject to the building permit requirement, owner oversight must be performed.

§ 99. Building design documentation and design specifications
(1) Design specifications are required for the creation of building design documentation concerning the building or extension of any road that is subject to the building permit requirement and that is mentioned in Annex 1 to this Code, provided the location of the road has not been identified by a spatial plan at the level of items of immovable property.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(2) The design specifications for the road - with the exception of national roads - are issued by the municipality together with the requirements for traffic arrangements. Design specifications for national roads are issued by the Transport Administration.
(2¹) Where design specifications are to be issued regarding a construction work for which both the municipality and the Transport Administration are competent to issue such specifications, the specifications are issued by the authority whose competence extends to the construction work that represents the majority of the envisaged solution.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(3) When connecting to an existing road or constructing utility network lines within the road area, the building design documentation must be approved by the owner of the road. The owner of the road may stipulate requirements, above all, in respect of:
1) materials;
2) measurements;
3) structural parameters;
4) technology;
5) the location – where not identified by the spatial plan or design specifications.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(4) The minister in charge of the policy sector enacts, by regulation, standards for the design of roads.

§ 100. Documentation of the building work performed on roads
The documents concerning building work performed on a national road must be handed over to the Transport Administration and the documents concerning building work performed on a local road must be handed over to the municipality.

§ 101. Building notice and building permit
(1) In order to perform building work on a road, a building notice is filed with the municipality, or the municipality issues a building permit.
(2) In order to build a national road or a national road envisaged by spatial plans, the building notice is filed with the Transport Administration, or the Transport Administration issues the building permit.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(2¹) Where a national designated spatial plan has been created for construction of a national road, the building permit to construct the road or any construction works connected to it is issued by the Transport Administration, or the building notice must be filed with the Transport Administration.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(2²) Where the building design documentation filed with the application for building permit concerning a road includes construction works for which both the municipality and the Transport Administration are competent to issue the permit, the permit is issued by the authority whose competence extends to the construction work that represents the majority of the envisaged solution.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(3) Where the road is to be built together with other construction works with which it forms a functional whole, the authority to issue the building permit may consolidate the proceedings concerning the issuing of the relevant building permits.

§ 101¹. Use and occupancy notice, use and occupancy permit
(1) Where a national designated spatial plan has been created mainly for construction of a national road, the use and occupancy permit for any construction works connected to construction of the road is issued by the Transport Administration, or the use and occupancy notice must be filed with the Transport Administration.
(2) Where the building design documentation filed with the application for use and occupancy permit includes construction works for which both the municipality and the Transport Administration are competent to issue the permit, the permit is issued by the authority whose competence extends to the construction work that represents the majority of the building design documentation.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]

§ 102. Audits
(1) The tasks of the competent entity provided for by Directive 2008/96/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on road infrastructure safety management (OJ L 319, 29.11.2008, pp. 59–67) are performed with regard to national roads by the Transport Administration and with regard to local roads by the municipality.
[RT I, 30.11.2021, 2 - entry into force 17.12.2021]
(1¹) Within the framework of the tasks provided for by subsection 1 of this section, the competent entity also arranges the performance of road safety impact assessments, road safety audits, network-wide road safety assessments and periodic road safety inspections with regard to:
1) roads that are part of the trans-European road network;
2) motorways and primary roads;
3) public-use roads built with funds from the European Union, except for roads providing access to a plot, pavements, foot paths, bicycle paths as well as foot and bicycle paths.
[RT I, 30.11.2021, 2 - entry into force 17.12.2021]
(2) The minister in charge of the policy sector enacts, by regulation:
1) the requirements for road safety impact assessments;
2) the requirements for road safety audits;
3) the requirements for network-wide road safety assessments;
4) the requirements for periodic road safety inspections;
5) the curriculum for road safety auditor training courses.
[RT I, 30.11.2021, 2 - entry into force 17.12.2021]

§ 103. Register of Roads
(1) The purpose of the Register of Roads is ensure the presence of a complete and up-to-date dataset on public roads for the organisation of road maintenance and for the exercise of regulatory enforcement.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(2) The constitutive regulations of the Register of Roads are enacted, by regulation, by the minister in charge of the policy sector; the regulations make provision for the rules for keeping the database, including, among other things:
1) the structure of the database;
2) the specific dataset;
3) data providers and the data to be received from them;
4) rules for the filing of data;
5) rules for access to and release of data;
6) specific time limits for data retention;
7) tasks of the controller;
8) other organisational matters related to the keeping of the database.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(3) The controller of the data in the Register of Roads is the Transport Administration.
(4) The information in the Register includes:
1) technical specifications of the road;
2) specifications concerning the civil engineering works required for the functioning of the road;
3) spatial data of the road;
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
4) particulars of the undertaking performing road maintenance – where requested by the road owner.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(5) The Register of Roads consists of:
1) the data of national roads;
2) the data of local roads;
3) the data of other roads – where requested by the road owner.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(6) [Repealed – RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(7) The owner of a road is obligated to file the particulars of the road within 30 days following acceptance of the road or following the issue of a use permit in respect of the road.
(8) The Constitutive Regulations may also provide for the possibility of other roads, which are not regulated in this part of the Code or in this Code, being registered in the Register of Roads.
(9) The information in the Register of Roads is disseminated through the Register's website.
(10) Data of the Register of Roads are retained for an unspecified period. The constitutive regulations of the register may provide shorter retention time limits.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]


Chapter 12 Construction Works in Public Water Bodies


Subchapter 1 Scope of Application

§ 104. Scope of application
(1) The provisions of this Chapter apply to the building of construction works in a public water body, and to encumbering such a water body with a construction work that does not have a permanent connection to the shore.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(2) Submerged cable lines, pipelines and other utility network lines and utility works that are connected to the shore, as well as construction works that are connected to the shore by means of submerged cable lines, pipelines and other utility network lines and utility works, are not deemed to constitute construction works that have a permanent connection to the shore.
(3) The provisions of this Chapter do not apply to the deepening of water bodies, to navigation signs and to the building of bridges that form a part of the road.
(4) Any monuments situated in public water bodies are subject to special rules provided by the Heritage Conservation Act.
(5) Where an offshore wind farm superficies licence provided for by subsection 1² of § 113¹ of this Code has been issued for the building of a construction work, building work does not require a building permit.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(6) A construction work built under an offshore wind farm superficies licence provided for by subsection 1² of § 113¹ of this Code is issued a use and occupancy permit if the construction work meets the requirements provided by legislation – first and foremost to those established for construction works – and to the offshore wind farm superficies licence provided for by the same subsection.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(7) The offshore wind farm superficies licence provided for by this Chapter is subject to provisions governing proceedings on superficies licences without prejudice to special rules provided by this Chapter.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]


Subchapter 2 Building a Construction Work in a Public Water Body

§ 105. Design specifications
(1) Design specifications for construction works to be situated in a public water body and to have a permanent connection to the shore are issued by the municipality within whose administrative territory the shoreline item of immovable property that is to support the building of the construction work is situated.
(2) Unless otherwise provided by law, design specifications are not required for creating building design documentation concerning construction works that do not have a permanent connection to the shore.
(3) Where this is needed, the municipality issues design specifications for the following construction works that do not have a permanent connection to the shore (hereinafter, construction work functionally connected to the shore):
1) a harbour facility required to service water craft, including any quays, protection moles or breakwaters;
2) a water traffic facility that is functionally connected to the harbour;
3) a utility network line or utility work required to service the construction works mentioned in clauses 1 and 2 of this subsection;
4) a civil engineering work that is to be situated in a public water body and that is required to service a construction work situated on the shore, except for any utility network lines or utility works that cross the national border or an administrative boundary between counties;
5) a sport or recreation facility that is envisaged without a permanent connection to the shore and that is to service a bathing beach;
6) to a construction work such as a floating hotel, sauna, restaurant or any other such work that serves persons arriving from the shore.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 106. Building notice
(1) In order to build, in a public water body, a construction work that has a permanent connection to the shore or that is functionally connected to the shore, a building notice is filed with the municipality.
(2) In order to build, in a public water body, a construction work that has no permanent connection to the shore, a building notice is filed with the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority.
(3) In order to build, in a public water body, a construction work that has no permanent connection to the shore, a superficies licence is filed together with the building notice.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 107. Authority competent to issue building permits
(1) The competent authority to issue the building permit for building, in a public water body, a construction work that has a permanent connection to the shore or that is functionally connected to the shore is the municipality.
(2) The competent authority to issue the building permit for building, in a public water body, a construction work that has no permanent connection to the shore is the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority.

§ 108. Application for a building permit
(1) Applications for a building permit concerning construction works that have a permanent connection to the shore or that have no such connection state, in addition to the particulars required under the General Part of this Code, the coordinates and surface area to be occupied by the construction work, or the coordinates and the surface area on which building work is to be performed.
(2) For a construction work that will not have a permanent connection to the shore and that is mentioned in clauses 1–4 of subsection 3 of § 105 of this Code, a superficies licence must be applied for in accordance with § 113³ of this Code before filing the application for a building permit.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(3) When filing an application for a building permit concerning a construction work that will not have a permanent connection to the shore, the requirements for applications for a superficies licence applicable by virtue of the General Part of this Code and by virtue of subsection 2 of § 113³ are followed.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(4) Where, in respect of the area identified in the application, other proceedings for the issue of a building permit or superficies licence have been opened, and the nature of the construction work to be built based on those proceedings is such as to rule out the issue, in respect of the area, of a second superficies licence, the competent authority may return the application for a building permit without considering it.

§ 109. Procedure for issuing building permits
(1) The competent authority may, by way of ancillary requirements to the building permit for a construction work that is to be situated in a public water body and that will not have a permanent connection to the shore, in addition to the requirements contained in the General Part of this Code, establish:
1) the time limit for demolishing the construction work and removing it from the public water body, and the related requirements, or
2) requirements connected to the use and operation mode of the construction work.
(2) The competent authority refuses to issue a building permit for a construction work that is to be situated in a public water body and that will, or will not, have a permanent connection to the shore, in addition to the requirements contained in the General Part of this Code, under the requirements provided by § 113³.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(3) [Repealed – RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 110. Use and occupancy notice
(1) In order to use and occupy a construction work that is situated in a public water body and that has a permanent connection to the shore or that is functionally connected to the shore, the use and occupancy notice is filed with the municipality.
(2) In order to use and occupy a construction work that is situated in a public water body and that does not have a permanent connection to the shore, a use and occupancy notice is filed with the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority.
(3) Where the building, in a public water body, of a construction work that has a permanent connection to the shore, led to a shift in the shoreline of the water body and to an increase in the surface area of the item of immovable property situated on the shore, the use and occupancy notice may be filed only after the shift of the shoreline and the increase of the item situated on the shore have been recorded in the Land Cadastre and in the Land Register.

§ 111. Authority competent to issue use and occupancy permits
(1) The competent authority to issue the use and occupancy permit in respect of a construction work that is situated in a public water body and has a permanent connection to the shore or that is functionally connected to the shore is the municipality.
(2) The competent authority to issue the use and occupancy permit in respect of a construction work that is situated in a public water body and has no permanent connection to the shore is the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority.

§ 112. Applications for the use and occupancy permit
Applications for the use and occupancy permit concerning construction works that have a permanent connection to the shore or that have no such connection state the coordinates and surface area of the area occupied by the construction work or of the area on which building work was performed.

§ 113. Procedure for issuing the use and occupancy permit
(1) The competent authority may, by way of ancillary requirements to the use and occupancy permit for a construction work that is situated in a public water body and that has or does not have a permanent connection to the shore, in addition to the requirements provided by the General Part of this Code, establish:
1) the time limit for demolishing the construction work and removing it from the public water body, and the related requirements, or
2) requirements related to the use and operation mode of the construction work.
(2) The competent authority refuses to issue the use and occupancy permit for a construction work that is situated in a public water body and that has or does not have a permanent connection to the shore, in addition to the requirements contained in the General Part of this Code, if the construction work:
1) contravenes the interests of national security;
2) may disturb air traffic, vessel traffic on shipping lanes or in a harbour, or disturb the safe mooring of water craft;
3) contravenes the conditions established in the superficies licence or
4) contravenes another public interest.
(3) Where the building, in a public water body, of a construction work that has a permanent connection to the shore, led to a shift in the shoreline of the water body and to an increase in the surface area of the item of immovable property situated on the shore, the use and occupancy permit is issued only after the shift of the shoreline and the increase of the item situated on the shore have been recorded in the Land Cadastre and in the Land Register and when, in accordance with the Water Act, the fee for encumbering a public water body with a construction work has been paid.
(4) The competent authority may refuse to issue the use and occupancy permit for a construction work that is situated in a public water body and that does not have a permanent connection to the shore if the applicant is not a person of a member state of the European Union or the European Economic Area.
(5) The use and occupancy permit for using and occupying a construction work that is situated in a public water body and that does not have a permanent connection to the shore is valid until expiry of the superficies licence on the basis of which the construction work was built, unless otherwise provided by the permit.


Subchapter 3 Encumbering a Public Water Body with a Construction Work that Does Not Have a Permanent Connection to the Shore

§ 113¹. Superficies licence
(1) ‘Superficies licence’ means a right to encumber, for a specified period of time, a delimited part of a public water body and of the exclusive economic zone with a construction work that is permanently connected to the bottom of the water body or to the seabed but does not have a permanent connection to the shore. The state is not required to apply for a superficies licence to encumber a public water body and the exclusive economic zone with a construction work.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(1¹) An application for a superficies licence to encumber a public water body with an offshore wind farm may be filed in respect of an area that constitutes at least 75 square kilometres.
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]
(1²) ‘Offshore wind farm superficies licence’ means a right to encumber, for a specified period of time, a delimited area in an inland sea, the territorial waters or the exclusive economic zone with a construction work that is permanently connected to the bottom of the water body or to the seabed, and provides a right to build an offshore wind farm that complies with the building design documentation based on which the superficies licence was issued, as well as a right to special use of water when building the wind farm.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(1³) The issuing of an offshore wind farm superficies licence rules out issuing a building permit and an environmental permit for special use of water (hereinafter, water permit) in relation to building the wind farm.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(2) A construction work that has been built under a superficies licence and that is covered by that licence constitutes an essential part of the licence and belongs to the holder of the licence as the holder's property. Any construction works that are permanently connected to the bottom of a public water body but do not have permanent connection to the shore and do not possess a superficies licence – or whose superficies licence has expired or has been revoked – constitute an essential part of the public water body and belong to the state as the state’s property.
(3) Unless otherwise provided by law, the superficies licence does not replace other permits prescribed by law that are required for building and using a construction work that constitutes an essential part of the licence.
(4) The area to be encumbered in the public water body is made up of the surface projection area of the construction work and of any civil engineering works required to service the construction work. Where construction works are built under a single superficies licence, the area to be encumbered is also deemed to include any distances of up to 1000 metres between the construction works, which are calculated based on the width dimension of the construction works. In the case of a wind power plant, the surface projection area is also deemed to include distances of up to 1000 metres between wind turbines that are part of the plant – calculated based on the width dimension of the turbines – as well as the ground projection area of any civil engineering works required to service the plant.
(5) This Subchapter does not apply to the dredging of public water bodies or to any navigation aids that are to be installed in such bodies.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 113². Superficies licence proceedings commenced by the state
(1) The state may apply for a superficies licence in order to encumber a public water body with:
1) an offshore wind farm;
2) a construction work intended to serve the purposes of an aquaculture-related commercial venture.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(2) Within 18 months following the issuing of the superficies licence, the state arranges a public auction or a selective tender to transfer the licence.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(3) When conducting the public auction or selective tender, the administrator of state assets or a person authorised by the administrator follows the State Assets Act without prejudice to special rules provided by this Code.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(4) Where the state files an application for a superficies licence, any other such applications that have been filed for the same water body area are returned by the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority (hereinafter in this Subchapter, the competent authority) without further consideration.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(5) Section 113⁶ does not apply in proceedings on an application for a superficies licence filed by the state.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(6) The rules for public auctions and selective tenders of superficies licences for public water bodies are enacted by a regulation of the Government of the Republic.
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]

§ 113³. Applying for a superficies licence
(1) The application for a superficies licence is filed with the competent authority.
(2) The application for a superficies licence must contain the following particulars:
1) the purpose of use of the construction work;
2) the maximum height and depth of the construction work and other technical particulars that are material in the case;
3) the number of construction works on the encumbered area and the ground projection area of the construction works;
4) the coordinates of the area to be encumbered in the public water body and the area's size in square metres;
5) where a public water body is to be encumbered with a power plant, the potential capacity of the plant and the system operator's technical requirements for its connection to the transmission network, except where the applicant is the system operator;
6) a list of envisaged investigations that the applicant intends to undertake in order for a decision to be made concerning the application;
7) the applied-for duration of the licence;
8) for a company or a non-profit association, a declaration certifying that the information filed with the Commercial Register or the Register of Non-Profit Associations and Foundations concerning the company's shareholders or members of the non-profit association, and its beneficial owners, is complete and accurate;
9) particulars concerning the sources of funding intended to finance the completion and subsequent use of the construction work that constitutes the subject matter of the licence;
10) where this is required by the competent authority, any other relevant information or documents related to the application;
11) information concerning the novelty of the technology envisaged to be employed in innovation areas.
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]
(3) A map of the layout of the envisaged construction work and of any civil engineering works required for servicing the construction work, including submerged cable lines, and any other documents material to deciding on encumbering the public water body with the construction work are annexed to the application. When the investigations and the environmental impact assessment – as determined by the competent authority - have been performed, the applicant files the investigation reports and the environmental impact assessment report with the authority. Where, on having conducted the investigations and environmental impact assessment, new specifics are included in the documents initially annexed to the application, the applicant files the documents anew.
(3¹) Within 180 days following the decision by which the environmental impact assessment report is found to meet the requirements, the applicant for an offshore wind farm superficies licence files, with the competent authority:
1) building design documentation that meets the requirements and technical particulars of the construction work – with the degree of detail sufficient for the granting of the right to build – and, where an expert assessment has been conducted concerning the building design documentation, also the expert assessment report;
2) particulars provided for by clauses 5–8 and 10–12 of subsection 1 of § 42 of the Act on the General Part of Environmental Code – unless such particulars have been sufficiently considered in the environmental impact assessment report;
3) particulars provided for by the regulation enacted under subsection 7 of § 42 of the Act on the General Part of Environmental Code concerning the dredging of a water body or deposition – including dumping – of solid substances in such a body.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(4) The minister in charge of the policy sector my, by regulation, enact a list of particulars to be stated in applications for a superficies licence as well as specific requirements for such applications and their annexes.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 113⁴. Initiating superficies licence proceedings
(1) Initiation of, or refusal to initiate, superficies licence proceedings is decided by the competent authority.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(2) Within the time limit provided by subsection 3 of § 113⁷, subsection 3 of § 113⁹ or subsection 4 of § 113¹¹ of this Code, the competent authority makes a decision to initiate – or refuse to initiate – superficies licence proceedings. Where this is justified, the authority has a right to extend the time limit.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(2¹) Superficies licence proceedings are initiated in the Register of Construction Works. Particulars and documents of the application are recorded in the Register by the competent authority.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 01.08.2024]
(3) When initiating superficies licence proceedings, the competent authority determines:
1) the person on whose application the proceedings are to be conducted;
2) whether or not to initiate environmental impact assessment;
3) where this is needed, any investigations that the applicant for the superficies licence must conduct for a decision to be made concerning the issuing of the licence, and the time limits for such investigations;
4) where this is needed, the requirements that are to be observed if other superficies licence proceedings have been initiated regarding the area identified in the application, or if - for a delimited area in the public water body named in the application - another valid superficies licence is present;
5) any other requirements that are needed.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(3¹) Where a water investigation mentioned in subsection 2 of § 236 of the Water Act is undertaken, the investigation is conducted following requirements provided by §§ 236, 237 and 243 of that Act. Where existing monitoring or investigation data are used, these must meet the requirements enacted under subsection 5 of § 53 of that Act.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(4) The competent authority may, on a reasoned application of the applicant for a superficies licence, extend the time limit for conducting any investigations or for complying with any other requirements determined on initiation of superficies licence proceedings.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(5) The statutory fee for the superficies licence is paid within 30 days following the decision to initiate superficies licence proceedings.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]

§ 113⁵. Opinion of the relevant authority
(1) The competent authority refers an application for a superficies licence to the relevant authorities for an opinion. The time limit for providing an opinion is 30 days. If, within the set time limit, the relevant authority has not provided and opinion or extended the time limit, the application may be disposed of without that authority's opinion.
(2) The relevant authority provides an opinion – in relation to the applicant and to the envisaged construction work – concerning their potential to endanger humans, property, the environment, national security, continuity of provision of a vital service, operation of the state's communications, a national defence object or the economy.
(3) The relevant authority may request - from any person and from the applicant - any documents or additional information that it needs in order to form its opinion.
(4) The relevant authority may propose that initiation of superficies licence proceedings be refused, where:
1) in the authority's assessment, a significant adverse impact to human life, health, the environment or property is present that it is not possible to sufficiently avoid or alleviate;
2) based on the authority's assessment of potential dangers involved, the applicant or the envisaged construction work poses a danger to national security, continuity of provision of a vital service, operation of the state's communications, a national defence object or the economy and it is not possible to avoid the danger;
3) the applicant has not, within the time limit set, produced the documents or additional information mentioned in subsection 3 of this section or made an application for the time limit to be extended;
4) the documents or additional information produced under subsection 3 of this section are inaccurate and the applicant has not cured their defects within 30 days following having been issued the corresponding requirement by the relevant authority.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 113⁶. Notice of application for a superficies licence
(1) Where the relevant authority does not, under subsection 4 of § 113⁵ of this Code, make a proposal to refuse initiation of the superficies licence and where circumstances provided for by subsections 1 and 2 of § 113¹¹ do not apply, the competent authority – prior to initiating superficies licence proceedings – publishes a notice in the official publication Ametlikud Teadaanded, in at least one daily newspaper of national circulation and on its website.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(2) The notice states the particulars of the applicant and of the application and – according to § 113⁷ of this Code – the rules and time limit for filing any parallel applications for a superficies licence.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(3) The application for a superficies licence is not subject to the provisions of subsections 1 and 2 of this section where:
1) the application has been filed by an applicant who has won the competition mentioned in § 28¹ of the Spatial Planning Act or has borne the costs of creating the national designated spatial plan for the same area;
2) the delimited area of the water body identified in the application is compatible with the location determined as the most suitable for constructing a wind farm in the national designated spatial plan that has been brought into effect and
3) no more than five years' time has elapsed following the bringing into effect of the national designated spatial plan.
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]
(4) The application for superficies licence is not subject to the provisions of subsections 1 and 2 of this section if it seeks to encumber a public water body with a submerged cable line, pipeline or other equivalent utility network or utility civil engineering work that has a connection to the shore.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]

§ 113⁷. Parallel application for a superficies licence
(1) Within 60 days following publication of the notice provided for by subsection 1 of § 113⁶ of this Code, an interested party has a right to file their own application for a superficies licence meeting the requirements provided for by § 113³ for encumbering the same delimited area of the public water body part with a construction work.
(2) Where consideration of the application suggests an absence of interest by any other parties in filing a parallel application for a superficies licence, the competent authority has a right to reduce – but not to less than 30 days – the time limit provided by subsection 1 of this section for the filing of such applications.
(3) If no parallel application for a superficies licence has been filed within the time limit stated in the notice provided for by subsection 1 of § 113⁶ of this Code, within 90 days following expiry of the time limit the competent authority makes a decision on initiating superficies licence proceedings. Where this is justified, the authority has a right to extend the time limit.
(4) Where a parallel application for a superficies licence is filed within the time limit stated in the notice published in accordance with subsection 2 of § 113⁶ of this Code and the construction work that the application envisages to encumber the delimited area of the public water body is substantially different from the construction work described in the first application, the competent authority, following the rules provided by § 113⁵ of this Code, refers the parallel application to the relevant authorities for an opinion.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 113⁸. Amending an application for a superficies licence
(1) Where the area to be encumbered in the public water body, as stated in the application for a superficies licence, is amended before a decision is made on initiating superficies licence proceedings. The competent authority requests an opinion from the relevant authorities following the rules provided by § 113⁵ of this Code. Where the amendment reduces the area to be encumbered, the competent authority may decide not to request such an opinion.
(2) Where this is justified, the area to be encumbered in the public water body – as stated in the application for a superficies licence – can be amended after the notice provided for by § 113⁶ of this Code has been published and the procedure provided for by § 113⁹ has taken place. Where, after publication of the notice, the location of the area is changed or the area is increased by more than 33 per cent, the competent authority publishes a new notice according to § 113⁶ of this Code and, if any parallel applications are filed, deals with these according to subsection 4 of § 113⁷ and § 113⁹.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 113⁹. Assessment of competing applications for a superficies licence
(1) Where more than one application has been filed with the competent authority concerning a delimited area in a public water body (hereinafter, competing application), in relation to which under § 113¹¹ no grounds apply for refusing to initiate superficies licence proceedings, the proceedings are initiated on the application that meets the aspects provided by subsection 2 of this section. If these aspects are met by several competing applications, a competitive tender provided for by subsection 1 of § 113¹⁰ of this Code is held. With respect to any other applications, the authority issues a refusal decision.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(2) The competent authority assesses competing applications having regard to:
1) the opinion of the relevant authority;
2) the guidelines and requirements stated in the relevant spatial plans;
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]
3) environmental considerations;
4) substance of the business activities of the applicant;
5) economic strength of the applicant;
6) economic profit that accrues to the state;
7) the period for erecting and using the construction work to be built on an area in a public water body;
8) the social usefulness of the project;
9) the purpose of use of the area in the public water body;
10) whether the project meets the aims provided for by the state's strategic documents;
11) the preferences of the state for use of the area in the public water body;
12) the novelty of the technology envisaged to be employed in the innovation area defined in the spatial plan.
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]
(3) The competent authority makes the decision by which it initiates or refuses to initiate superficies licence proceedings within 90 days following approval of the results of assessment of applications for a superficies licence. Where this is justified, the authority has a right to extend the time limit.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(4) [Repealed – RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]

§ 113¹⁰. Initiating superficies licence proceedings by competitive tender
(1) Where no refusal decision has been made under subsection 1 of § 113⁹ of this Code, the competent authority – within 60 days following approval of the results of assessment of the applications – arranges an auction-based competitive tender (hereinafter, competitive tender) between the parties who filed the competing applications.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(2) When it announces a competitive tender, the competent authority determines:
1) the starting price for the auction, set at 12,500 euros per square kilometre where the public water body is to be encumbered with a construction work that does not have a permanent connection to the shore but that is not an offshore wind farm, and at 15,000 euros per square kilometre where the public water body is to be encumbered with a wind power plant;
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]
2) the amount of the deposit fee, which is two per cent of the starting price in the case of offshore wind farms and ten per cent in the case of other construction works;
3) whether the competitive tender is held as an oral, written or electronic auction;
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]
4) the requirements for bids.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(3) The deposit fee is returned once the winner has emerged or the tender has been declared unsuccessful. The winner's deposit is deducted from the bid made in the auction.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(4) The deposit fee is not returned to a person who caused the auction to be declared unsuccessful under clause 2 or 3 of subsection 7 of this section.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(5) The competent authority does not admit to the competitive tender - as a participant in that tender - an applicant who filed a competing application if they have not paid the deposit fee within the time limit.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(6) The competent authority rejects a bid made by a participant if the bid does not comply with the requirements.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(7) The competent authority declares a competitive tender unsuccessful where:
1) the rules for conducting the tender have been violated;
2) after the tender has taken place, it comes to light that the winner has filed false information;
3) - when the winner does not, within the time limit, pay the amount they have bid or withdraws their application for a superficies licence - only one bid remains that complies with the requirements;
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
4) no person has been registered as participant of the auction;
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
5) no bids – or no bids that comply with requirements – have been filed;
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
6) at the auction, an arrangement between, or concerted activity of, participants came to light, which materially affected – or may have materially affected – the result of the auction;
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
7) other circumstances mentioned by the organiser in the terms or notice of the auction come to light.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(8) Where a competitive tender is declared unsuccessful, the competent authority may arrange a new competitive tender within 30 days following the day on which the bids were opened. If the new tender is unsuccessful, the tender ends without a result.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(9) The person who filed a competing application and whose actions or omissions caused the competitive tender to be declared unsuccessful is not allowed to participate in a new competitive tender arranged under subsection 8 of this section and, with respect to their application, the competent authority makes a decision by which it refuses to initiate superficies licence proceedings.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(10) Superficies licence proceedings are initiated for the participant of the competitive tender who has bid the highest price in that tender and who, within the time limit determined in the notice of the tender, pays the amount they have bid.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(11) [Repealed – RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(12) Based on subsection 10 of this section, the competent authority ascertains the applicant for whom superficies licence proceedings are to be initiated, and – within 90 days following the applicant’s having been ascertained – makes a decision by which it initiates such proceedings. With respect to any other competing applications, the authority – within the same time limit – enters a decision by which it refuses to initiate the proceedings. Where this is justified, the authority may extend the time limit.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(13) Where circumstances provided for by § 113¹¹ of this Code come to light, superficies licence proceedings that were initiated by competitive tender may end with a refusal to issue the licence.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]
(14) The rules for initiating superficies licence proceedings by competitive tender are enacted by a regulation of the minister in charge of the policy sector.
[RT I, 07.03.2023, 21 - entry into force 17.03.2023]

§ 113¹¹. Refusing to initiate superficies licence proceedings
(1) Where it is manifest that it is impossible to issue a superficies licence, the competent authority refuses to initiate superficies licence proceedings.
(2) The competent authority also refuses to initiate superficies licence proceedings where:
1) for the delimited area of the water body that is described in the application, proceedings have already been initiated for the issue of another superficies licence, and it is not possible to issue a second superficies licence for the area due to the nature of the construction work to be built under the superficies licence that may be issued as a result of such proceedings;
2) the application is contrary to a spatial plan that is in effect for the delimited area of the water body that is described in the application;
3) a spatial planning proceedings have been initiated in respect of the delimited area of the water body described in the application, and have not been completed;
4) a national designated spatial plan must be adopted in order to build the envisaged construction work;
5) a significant adverse impact for human life, health, the environment or property is present that cannot be sufficiently avoided or alleviated;
6) the applicant or a person connected to the applicant or the envisaged construction work creates a danger to national security, to continuity of provision of a vital service, to operation of the state's communications, to a national defence object or the economy and the danger cannot be eliminated;
7) regarding the applicant, circumstances are present that are provided for by clause 3 or 4 of subsection 4 of § 113⁵ or by the third sentence of subsection 1 of § 113⁹ or by subsection 9 or the second sentence of subsection 12 of § 113¹⁰ or by clause 2, 4 or 6 of subsection 1 or by subsection 3 of § 113¹³ of this Code;
8) the competitive tender arranged on the basis of § 113¹⁰ of this Code has ended without a result.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(3) The provision of clause 3 of subsection 2 of this section does not apply to a construction work provided for by subsection 2 of § 104 of this Code and to a temporary construction work if the applicant accepts that the superficies licence will be issued for the period of validity provided by subsection 4 of § 113¹⁴.
(4) Unless otherwise provided for by this Code, within 90 days following emergence of a circumstance provided for by subsection 2 of this section the competent authority makes a decision by which it refuses to initiate superficies licence proceedings. Where this is justified, the authority has a right to extend that time limit.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 113¹². Issuing a superficies licence
(1) A superficies licence is issued by the competent authority electronically, in the Register of Construction Works.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 01.08.2024]
(2) When issuing a superficies licence, the following conditions of the licence are determined:
1) the licence holder;
2) the coordinates and size in square metres of the encumbered area in the public water body, including the area to be taken up by the envisaged construction work;
3) the location of the construction work in the area encumbered;
4) the purpose of use of the construction work;
5) the maximum authorised height and depth as well as any other important technical particulars of the construction work;
6) the maximum authorised number of construction works and the maximum ground projection area that is authorised for a construction work;
7) the validity period of the licence;
8) restrictions on using the licence;
9) any other necessary requirements.
(2¹) In addition to conditions mentioned in subsection 2 of this section, conditions provided for by clauses 5 and 6 of subsection 3 of § 42 and of clause 2 of subsection 1 of § 109 of this Code, as well as by clauses 5–10, 12 and 15 of subsection 1 of § 193 of the Water Act may be set for the offshore wind farm superficies licence.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(2²) The competent authority presents the particulars and documents provided for by subsection 3¹ of § 113³ of this Code to the Environment Board for conditions to be set for the special use of water. The Board presents the conditions in writing within 30 days following reception of particulars and documents.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(2³) Having received the conditions provided for by subsection 2² of this section, the competent authority presents a proposal for the offshore wind farm superficies licence:
1) for approval to the authority that, under legislation, holds competences relating to the subject matter of the building or water permit;
2) where this is needed, for an opinion to a person whose rights or interests may be affected by the construction work or its building.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(2⁴) Where the authority or person has not, within 30 days of having received the proposal for the offshore wind farm superficies licence, refused to approve it or expressed an opinion, and has not requested an extension of the time limit, the authority is deemed to have tacitly approved the proposal or the person to have declined to express an opinion concerning it – unless otherwise provided for by law.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(2⁵) The offshore wind farm superficies licence is issued within 90 days following the filing of particulars and documents mentioned in subsection 3¹ of § 113³ of this Code.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(3) In the course of superficies licence proceedings, based on the results of environmental impact assessment and of any investigations that have been conducted, the location of the area to be encumbered in a public water body may – by reference to the coordinates stated and compared to the area determined in the decision by which the proceedings were initiated – be modified, or the area may be increased, by up to 33 per cent, or reduced to a greater extent. The location of the area must not be modified or increased such that it comes to encompass a location for which a superficies licence has been issued or regarding which proceedings for issuing another superficies licence have been initiated, and it is not possible to realise both licences concurrently.
(3¹) In superficies licence proceedings that do not include an assessment of environmental impact or the conduct of investigations, the making of changes provided for by subsection 3 of this section is permitted in other situations where this is justified.
[RT I, 11.07.2026, 3 – entry into force 01.08.2026]
(4) The competent authority requests the opinion of the relevant authority under the rules provided by § 113⁵ of this Code concerning any increase of or modification of location to the area to be encumbered in a public water body where such increase or modification exceeds 33 per cent.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 113¹³. Refusing to issue a superficies licence
(1) The competent authority refuses to issue a superficies licence where:
1) the applicant has not fulfilled the requirements set in the decision to initiate superficies licence proceedings and has not applied for a new time limit for fulfilling these;
2) the conditions of the licence applied for are contrary to a superficies licence that is in effect;
3) the conditions of the licence applied for are contrary to a spatial plan that is in effect;
4) the conditions of the licence applied for are contrary to the state's security interests;
5) there is a significant negative environmental impact that cannot be sufficiently avoided or alleviated;
6) the construction work that constitutes an essential part of the licence would interfere with air traffic, with vessel traffic in a fairway or port basin or with the safe berthing of water craft;
7) based on the results of superficies licence proceedings, the area to be encumbered in the public water body needs to be modified and the applicant does not accept the modifications.
(1¹) When issuing an offshore wind farm superficies licence, the grounds of refusal provided by clauses 1–3 of § 44 of this Code apply in addition to those stated in subsection 1 of this section.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(1²) When issuing an offshore wind farm superficies licence, the grounds of refusal to issue the permit provided by clauses 8–10 of subsection 3 of § 192 of the Water Act may be applied.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(2) The competent authority may also refuse to issue a superficies licence where reasonable doubts are present that the applicant, a person connected with the applicant or the envisaged construction work may endanger national security, continuity of provision of a vital service, operation of the state’s communications, a national defence object or the economy, or where the applicant for an offshore wind farm superficies licence has not complied with an obligation emanating from subsection 3¹ of § 113³ of this Code and has not offered a valid reason to extend the time limit.
[RT I, 11.06.2024, 1 - entry into force 21.06.2024]
(3) The competent authority may refuse to issue a superficies licence to a person who is not a citizen or legal person of Estonia or of a state party to the European Economic Area and whose superficies licence application is not aligned with material interests of the state.
[RT I, 27.04.2022, 1 - entry into force 07.05.2022]

§ 113¹⁴. Period of validity of a superficies licence
(1) A superficies licence is valid for up to 50 years. When determining the period of validity, the competent authority has regard to the type and purpose of use of the construction work.
(2) The competent authority may, on an application of the licence holder, extend a superficies licence by up to 50 years. An application for extending the licence is filed at least three months before expiry of the licence period.
(3) Extending the period of validity of a superficies licence is subject to the provisions of § 113¹⁵ of this Code.
(4) Where an application for a superficies licence is filed regarding an area in respect of which a spatial planning exercise has been initiated and the proceedings have not been concluded, the competent authority may issue a provisional superficies licence. The provisional licence is reviewed within one year following the bringing of the spatial plan into effect.
